title: Ways a game is drawn (part 4 of 4)
outcomes: Lists the ways a game can end drawn and says which can be claimed and which are automatic
Says when a position has occurred for the third time, and what must match (same side to move, same rights)
Counts the fifty-move clock and says what resets it (a capture or a pawn move, not a check)
Says when repeating a position helps (the side that is behind) and when it throws away an advantage

steps.text: Part 4 of 4: Ways a game is drawn. This part covers Check yourself. Each part is short on purpose: finish one, play a game or take a break, and come back.

**Say it back.** A position has repeated only when the pieces, whose turn it is and the rights all match, and the third time lets a player claim a draw. The half-move count resets after a capture or a pawn move, not after a check, and at 100 a player may claim. [H] A side with a winning plan usually changes the plan; a side with no way to make progress may be happy to repeat.

steps.prompt: Explain to a friend in three sentences why the third repeat lets you claim a draw, and why a check does not reset the 50-move count.
